abstract: People increasingly form meaningful relationships with conversational AI. Current variable-centered literature offers a mixed picture of relational patterns and how they associate with wellbeing. Taking a person-centered approach, we applied latent profile analysis to secondary data from 467 active conversational AI users, evaluating five indicators of machine companionship: utilitarian motivation, eudaimonic exchange, connective coordination, mind perception, and inclusion of other in the self. Five profiles emerged, ordering parsimoniously from objectified-utilitarian to intimate-bonded. Conceptually divergent utilitarian motivation and companionate engagement co-occurred, rather than diverging. Furthermore, deep companionship was achieved without users attributing a mind to the AI. Profile membership was strongly associated with relatedness need satisfaction, tracking upward across the groups, but was only weakly associated with loneliness, indicating AI fulfills immediate relational needs but may not resolve systemic human disconnection. Ultimately, these findings characterize human-AI relationships as graded configurations spanning a superordinate continuum of self-expansion

ur.ai_reason: 基于467名用户数据分析AI陪伴及幸福感
ur.tldr: 对467名活跃对话式AI用户进行潜在剖面分析，识别出从工具化到亲密联结的五类人机陪伴模式。工具动机与陪伴投入可并存，深度陪伴不依赖赋予AI心智；相关感满足随剖面上升，但与孤独感的关联较弱，说明AI能即时满足关系需求，却难消解结构性孤独。

title: Self-Expansion Through AI: Latent Profile Analysis of AI Companionship and Wellbeing Outcomes
title_zh: 通过 AI 实现自我扩展：AI 陪伴与福祉结果的潜在剖面分析
